fixes.explanation: Yes, friend, cities with pasturelands around them. The LORD tells Moses to have Israel give them from the inheritance the people will possess (Numbers 35:2). The Levites get homes and room for their herds and flocks. That fits what the LORD said earlier, that the Levites would receive no inheritance among the Israelites (Numbers 18:23-24). So the other tribes share what they have, and the Levites aren't left out.

I get the guess, since the LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab, across from Jericho (Numbers 35:1). But He never names a valley for the Levites. He asks for cities to live in and pasturelands around them, given from the inheritance of the tribes (Numbers 35:2). One big valley would be easier to hand over, but that's not the order. It's cities, spread out.

Yes, friend, the assembly. The city of refuge keeps the avenger from reaching the manslayer first. His case goes before the assembly, so nothing gets settled on the road (Numbers 35:12). The city is where he stays safe until then.

That's it, friend. This is the case where the killing was not done in hostility. The assembly takes the manslayer's side against the avenger of blood (Numbers 35:25). Then it sends him back to the city of refuge he fled to, and he lives there until the high priest dies.

The text goes the opposite direction, friend. For the one who killed by accident, the assembly stands between him and the avenger of blood (Numbers 35:25). Nothing there has the assembly giving him up. Instead it returns him to the city of refuge he fled to.

That's the reason the text gives. Then the LORD says, “Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.” (Numbers 35:34) The land matters because He lives among His people. Just before this, He says bloodshed pollutes the land (Numbers 35:33). I think that's a lot to take in, and it shows how seriously He treats life.
